rounds.text: Shiv Om Investment & Consultancy Ltd is currently trading at a profound discount to its intrinsic value, evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of just 0.14x [E2] and a P/E ratio of 1.02 [E1]. While the market has priced the company at a mere ₹ 2.94 Cr [E3], the firm has demonstrated a strong ability to generate returns for shareholders, evidenced by an ROE of 17.8% [E6]. This profitability is further underscored by a robust 67% compounded profit growth over the last five years [E12] and a 27% growth rate over the last three years [E13]. Conceded: the company has seen a decline in sales growth over the long term [E7, E8, E42] and a recent contraction in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E14]. Despite these headwinds, the company maintains a consistent 10% compounded profit growth over the decade [E11]. Conceded: the company does not currently provide a dividend yield to investors [E4] and maintains a modest ROCE of 6.8% [E5].

The valuation metrics of Shiv Om Investment & Consultancy Ltd suggest a deep-value trap rather than a bargain, as the company suffers from a persistent inability to grow its top line [E7], [E8], [E42]. While the low P/E and price-to-book ratios appear attractive [E1], [E2], these figures are undermined by a complete lack of dividend payments to shareholders [E4]. The company’s operational efficiency is questionable, evidenced by a mediocre ROCE of only 6.8% [E5]. Furthermore, the recent trend in profitability is alarming, with a 22% decline in profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14]. Conceded: [E6], [E12], [E13]. Investors must weigh the statistical cheapness against the reality of long-term sales contraction and recent earnings volatility [E7], [E14].
